title: Build a Task Manager with Persistent Storage
prompt: Create, list, complete, and remove tasks, then save and reload them from a local file with error handling. Follow the acceptance criteria and include the expected behavior in a short README or code comment.
objective: Create, list, complete, and remove tasks, then save and reload them from a local file with error handling.

starter.code:
// TODO: define the types and error behavior first.

expected_output: A Rust implementation that satisfies the acceptance criteria and passes its local cargo test suite; verify the output and failure paths in the declared environment.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation addresses the stated task and represents the relevant data clearly.
The core operation is separated into readable functions or types where that improves maintainability.
At least one normal input and one edge/failure case are tested.
No secrets or real personal data are included; external effects use synthetic data or controlled test doubles.
The learner documents design decisions and any static-grader limitations.
hints: Write down the input, output, and failure cases before coding.
Build the smallest correct version, then test boundary cases.
Use cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo test; static token checks do not prove full correctness.
grading_method: Static required-token smoke check only. This is not Rust execution and does not prove compilation or runtime correctness; run the project locally with Cargo and use human review for advanced, database, FFI, async, embedded, and WebAssembly work.
retry_policy: Allow retries. Completion and XP decisions remain under platform backend rules; this file defines no XP override.
status_note: Draft based on Section C of Rust.pdf; inspect the Rust starter, grading tokens, hidden reference solution, and target/dependency requirements before publication.
